query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but its poor oxygen resistance limits practical high-temperature use. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing the alloy’s useful mechanical performance? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention and mechanism, the predicted change relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr, the relevant temperature, atmosphere, exposure time, and mechanical-loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Aluminum addition improves the oxidation resistance of equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr without sacrificing its mechanical performance.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr in the cast state
generation.conditions: Room temperature and elevated temperatures up to 1000 °C
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a protective oxide layer
generation.mechanism: Aluminum reacts with oxygen to form a stable and dense oxide layer, reducing the oxidation rate of the alloy
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved oxidation resistance and retained mechanical properties, including yield strength and tensile ductility
generation.boundary: Temperature range: 25 °C to 1000 °C, atmosphere: air, exposure time: up to 100 hours, mechanical loading: tensile testing
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of aluminum addition required to achieve optimal oxidation resistance without compromising mechanical properties is uncertain

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing and oxidation resistance evaluation of Al-added HfNbTaTiZr at elevated temperatures
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of aluminum does not improve the oxidation resistance of HfNbTaTiZr without sacrificing its mechanical performance, the hypothesis is falsified
